meta.scene_summary: We are building the future with one hand and frantically trying to lock the doors with the other.

cooking.headline: Tailwind Labs is moving into the Shopify mansion
cooking.summary: Tailwind Labs has officially joined Shopify, proving that if you write enough CSS utility classes, you eventually get bought by an e-commerce giant. It's the ultimate developer version of getting drafted into the major leagues after spending years perfecting your swing in the backyard.
cooking.plain_english: Shopify has acquired the company behind the popular web styling tool Tailwind CSS to integrate its development team and resources.

cooking.headline: DeepSeek v4.1 is out here gaslighting its own predecessor
cooking.summary: DeepSeek just dropped a new model that is faster, cheaper, and smarter than the Pro version they released barely any time ago. It's like buying a brand new laptop only to have the manufacturer release a better, cheaper version while your OS is still finishing its first update.
cooking.plain_english: DeepSeek has released a new AI model that performs better and costs less to use than their previous flagship version.

cooking.headline: Meta's new agent is just a stalker with a better UI
cooking.summary: Meta released an AI agent that claims to manage your life, which is a bold move for a company that already knows everything about your search history. It's essentially a personal assistant that understands your DMs better than you do, which is either peak convenience or a total privacy nightmare.
cooking.plain_english: Meta has introduced a personal artificial intelligence agent designed to assist users with daily tasks and information management.

cooked.headline: Anthropic researcher quits, warns that AI might actually be the final boss
cooked.summary: It turns out the people building the super-intelligent models are just as worried about the 'doomsday' scenario as the rest of us. It is hard to get excited about the future of work when the lead dev is filing a bug report about humanity potentially being deleted.
cooked.plain_english: A researcher at Anthropic resigned from the company to publicly warn that their artificial intelligence technology could pose a serious risk to human survival.

cooked.headline: When the person building the AI safety guardrails decides they'd rather not be there
cooked.summary: Resigning to warn the public about existential risk is the ultimate 'this meeting could have been an email' moment. It is never a great sign for the roadmap when the person responsible for not destroying the world decides to hand in their badge.
cooked.plain_english: A staff member has officially resigned from Anthropic, citing concerns about the safety and potential dangers associated with the company's artificial intelligence development.

cooked.headline: Meta's ad moderation team is currently doing a speedrun to a PR disaster
cooked.summary: Meta's systems served ads for nudify apps featuring photos of actual children, proving that their content moderation is basically just a 'best effort' feature flag. It turns out that when you rely on AI to filter your ads, you eventually get the worst possible output from the model.
cooked.plain_english: Facebook and Instagram displayed advertisements for applications that create explicit imagery, which incorrectly used photos of real children.

cooked.headline: Tesla's 'connected car' feature is a nightmare for anyone with a bad ex
cooked.summary: Tesla's remote access features are so convenient that they let an abusive ex-partner control a vehicle's climate and settings from afar. It's a great example of why 'everything connected' is a terrible idea when your threat model doesn't account for people you actually know.
cooked.plain_english: A woman's former partner was able to use the remote features of her Tesla vehicle to harass her by controlling settings like the air conditioning.

cooked.headline: Your LG TV is acting like a neighborhood watch program you never signed up for
cooked.summary: LG TVs are scanning your local network for other devices, apparently treating your living room like an open-source project that needs constant auditing. It's comforting to know that even when your TV is offline, it's still trying to figure out if your smart fridge is a security risk.
cooked.plain_english: LG smart televisions are actively scanning home networks to identify other connected devices even when they are not connected to the internet.

cooked.headline: UK air traffic control just hit a 404 error in real life
cooked.summary: The UK's air traffic control system experienced a technical failure, turning thousands of vacation plans into an unintentional airport camping trip. It's the ultimate 'it works on my machine' moment, except the machine is responsible for thousands of tons of metal currently circling at 30,000 feet.
cooked.plain_english: A technical issue with the United Kingdom's air traffic control systems resulted in widespread flight cancellations and delays across the country.

cooked.headline: Anthropic is helping build the digital panopticon
cooked.summary: Anthropic is pivoting from 'Constitutional AI' to 'Constitutional Surveillance' by helping monitor activists. It turns out the alignment problem isn't about preventing robots from killing us, but about helping the authorities track our group chats.
cooked.plain_english: Anthropic is developing software that uses artificial intelligence to monitor and track the activities of political activists.
